is_anopheles.evidence: The study uses laboratory strains of Anopheles arabiensis.

reports_target_markers.evidence: The study reports genotyping for Vgsc L995F (kdr-west) and L995S (kdr-east) on page 5.

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: The paper states: 'All SENN-DDT samples assayed for the L1014F mutation were homozygous resistant (L1014F/F)... All SENN adults were homozygous susceptible (wild-type L1014L/L)' (page 5).

african_field_population.evidence: The study uses laboratory-reared strains (SENN and SENN-DDT) maintained in an insectary in Johannesburg, South Africa. The SENN strain was originally colonized from Sudan in 1980 (page 2).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is an empirical laboratory study.

sub_country_location.evidence: The study uses laboratory colonies, not field-collected mosquitoes.

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: The study uses laboratory colonies, not field-collected mosquitoes.

duplicate_risk.evidence: This is a laboratory-based study using established colonies.

supplement.evidence: All necessary data is provided in the main text.

assessment.summary: This study examines the effect of larval nutritional deprivation on the life history and DDT resistance phenotype in laboratory-reared Anopheles arabiensis strains (SENN and SENN-DDT). It finds that larval starvation leads to smaller adults with reduced DDT tolerance and lower detoxification enzyme activity. The study is ineligible because it uses laboratory colonies rather than field-collected African populations.
exclusion_reasons: The study uses laboratory colonies, not field-collected African populations.
